points.requirement: Explain T-cell antigen recognition, IFNg signaling, induced PD-L1 and PD-1-mediated restraint of the response.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Explain T-cell antigen recognition, IFNg signaling, induced PD-L1 and PD-1-mediated restraint of the response.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The sequence proposed by Taube and colleagues and mapped in more detail since is a loop. A T cell recognises a tumour peptide on HLA and releases interferon gamma; the interferon acts through the Janus kinases JAK1 and JAK2 in nearby tumour and immune cells; PD-L1 rises; PD-L1 binds PD-1 on the T cell and damps it. In melanoma cell lines, Garcia-Diaz and colleagues found that the interferon gamma, JAK1 and JAK2, STAT1, STAT2 and STAT3, IRF1 axis primarily regulates PD-L1, with IRF1 binding the PD-L1 promoter, and biopsies from patients with melanoma showed enrichment of that interferon signature and of STAT and IRF1 target genes in tumours that responded to anti-PD-1 treatment.

points.requirement: Distinguish induced expression from tumor-intrinsic constitutive expression independent of local T-cell induction.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Distinguish induced expression from tumor-intrinsic constitutive expression independent of local T-cell induction.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Evidence from tissue. In human melanocytic lesions, 98% of PD-L1-positive (B7-H1-positive) tumours had tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes compared with 28% of PD-L1-negative tumours; positive melanocytes sat almost always immediately next to lymphocytes, and interferon gamma was detected at the interface but not in PD-L1-negative tumours (Taube and colleagues). The same colocalisation appeared in inflamed benign naevi, which fits PD-L1 as a response to tissue inflammation. In triple-negative breast cancer, Gruosso and colleagues described an immunoreactive group whose tumours had granzyme B-positive CD8 T cells inside cancer-cell regions, a type 1 interferon signature and elevated IDO and PD-L1, the pattern adaptive resistance predicts; that is an association in tissue and not a direct test of the loop. The alternative, called innate or constitutive resistance, is PD-L1 driven by the cancer cell's own signalling regardless of T cells.

points.requirement: Separate human inflamed-melanoma PD-L1/IDO/Treg association from mouse CD8-dependent IFNg induction and chemokine Treg recruitment.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Separate human inflamed-melanoma PD-L1/IDO/Treg association from mouse CD8-dependent IFNg induction and chemokine Treg recruitment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: PD-L1 is not the only brake that follows the attack. Spranger and colleagues found in human melanoma that the T-cell-inflamed tumours were the ones with high indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), PD-L1 and regulatory T cells, and in mice that all three depended on CD8 T cells being present: IDO and PD-L1 through interferon gamma, and regulatory T cells through CCR4-binding chemokines with some induced proliferation. Their reading was that these pathways are driven by the immune response rather than orchestrated by the cancer cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the loop means for treatment is a hypothesis to test. PD-1 and PD-L1 drugs interrupt the last step, the binding of PD-L1 to PD-1. points.requirement: Loss of inducible IFNg response can remove induced PD-L1 and presentation changes without necessarily removing baseline recognition.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Loss of inducible IFNg response can remove induced PD-L1 and presentation changes without necessarily removing baseline recognition.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A functionally important loss of JAK1 or JAK2 can impair the tumour cell response to interferon gamma. In four people with metastatic melanoma that relapsed on anti-PD-1 treatment, two relapse samples carried loss-of-function JAK1 or JAK2 mutations with deletion of the remaining normal allele, and truncating JAK1 or JAK2 mutations left the cells unresponsive to interferon gamma (Zaretsky and colleagues). The JAK2-deficient relapse cells lost interferon-gamma-induced PD-L1 and class-I increases but retained responses to interferon alfa and beta. In engineered melanoma cells, JAK1 or JAK2 loss did not abolish recognition by the tested NY-ESO-1-specific T cells. Loss of inducibility is therefore different from absence of all baseline recognition. This selected series does not estimate a frequency for all cancers.

points.requirement: A negative or patchy PD-L1 score does not establish absence of immune attack or other inhibitory mechanisms.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: A negative or patchy PD-L1 score does not establish absence of immune attack or other inhibitory mechanisms.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading the label. PD-L1-positive does not mean the tumour is suppressing the immune system on its own, because in adaptive resistance the signal is a reaction to T cells. PD-L1-negative does not mean no immune attack: staining is patchy, assays differ and other brakes exist. Adaptive resistance also differs from acquired resistance, which means a tumour that responded to treatment and then stopped responding; here 'adaptive' names an induced defence, and the two can overlap without being the same thing.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: A negative or patchy PD-L1 score does not establish absence of immune attack or other inhibitory mechanisms.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional biopsy, PD-L1 is found at a lymphocyte-rich border but not at the centre. That distribution is consistent with induced expression; it does not prove the proposed loop. A negative region does not establish absence of immune attack elsewhere, and other inhibitory pathways may operate. A positive PD-L1 result alone also cannot distinguish induced from constitutive expression.

evidence.explanation: This exact reader passage represents the specified distinction, measurement, study or qualified inference: Spatial colocalization and IFNg-expression programs suggest induction; a PD-L1 score alone does not identify its cause.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A PD-L1 stain measures protein on defined tumour and immune cells, not why it is present. Colocalization with lymphocytes and interferon-related expression can support induced expression, while a uniform lymphocyte-poor pattern raises other hypotheses; neither pattern proves a cause. Adding interferon gamma and measuring PD-L1 tests inducibility in a laboratory model. Appropriate pathway perturbations and controls investigate causation, and neither that assay nor a tissue score measures the entire in-vivo feedback loop or treatment benefit.
